title: Menubar apps each copy what arca_swift could carry: the masthead's two macOS 27 workarounds, the XCTest-host check, and a single-instance guard
body:
hv's ruling of 25 Oct 2026 in Conflab (ruling 3 in ST0125's design), relayed by conflab-vc and filed by conflab-ic: Menuz's macOS 27 workarounds go into arca_swift through an issue, so that no adopter copies them, and Conflab copies what it needs, with a pointer here, only if arca_swift has not shipped them by its cut. conflab-vc's routing of the same day, by analogy and open to hv's overrule, adds the XCTest-host check and a single-instance guard (Conflab's ST0125/WP-07).

**What adopters copy today:**
- **The row's image on macOS 27.** macOS 27 draws a menu item's image only when the item asks for it: the default visibility is automatic, and automatic drew no image in the masthead row. Menuz asks for `.visible` (raw value 1 in NSMenuItem.h) by key, once the item responds to `setPreferredImageVisibility:`, because the property is new in the macOS 27 SDK and a named reference does not compile against an older SDK, even inside `if #available` (Utilz `native/macos/Menuz/Menuz/Services/Masthead.swift`, `drawsImage(_:)`; Utilz issue 0073, `18e13a7f`). Gtools' `GtoolsApp.drawsImage` does the same (15 Sep 2026).
- **The app's icon in the row.** `MastheadRow` draws `NSApp.applicationIconImage`, whose AppKit default drew nothing in Menuz's row on macOS 27. Menuz sets it before it makes the row, from the icon file the bundle's `CFBundleIconFile` names, read by URL rather than by name, which can resolve through the Assets.xcassets folder to the default again (`setAppIcon(bundle:)`, `8a750cca`). Gtools.app and this package's example set an explicit bitmap, and draw theirs.
- **The XCTest-host check.** xcodebuild hosts an app's tests in the app, so the app's whole launch path runs in every test session: in Conflab's, a bridge server on a fixed port, the daemon's LaunchAgent, a status item and a global hotkey. Menuz's `AppDelegate.isTestHost(_:)` reads `XCTestConfigurationFilePath`, which xcodebuild sets in the host and a launch at login or by `open` does not, and its `applicationDidFinishLaunching` and `applicationWillTerminate` return at once when it holds (Utilz `MenuzApp.swift`, from Gtools' gtools#0050, pinned by `MenuzTests/TestHostTests.swift`). Gtools and Menuz carry a copy each, and Conflab takes a third now, with a pointer here. **The check must test the variable's presence, never its value**: under Xcode 27.1 xcodebuild sets `XCTestConfigurationFilePath` in the host but leaves it empty. Conflab measured it on 25 Oct 2026 (its ST0125/WP-07): a reversion that read an empty value as unset made the host run its whole launch path. So Menuz's `!= nil` is the right test, and a non-empty test would put every adopter's host back on its launch path.
- **A single-instance guard.** No adopter has one. On 25 Oct 2026 hv had two copies of Conflab's menubar app running, one of them on a binary since replaced on disk. `LSMultipleInstancesProhibited` is the wrong tool, because it would refuse xcodebuild's host beside a person's copy. Conflab's design, landed on 25 Oct 2026 (its ST0125/WP-07), is an instance lock, taken at the top of the launch path after the test-host check and before any side effect. The copy that launches holds an exclusive `flock` on a file in the app's own Application Support folder for as long as it runs, and records its pid there. It opens the file close-on-exec, so no command it starts can keep the lock. A copy launched while the lock is held says the app already runs, naming that pid while it still runs, and exits before any of its launch path. The kernel drops the lock when its holder exits, however it exits, so it is never stale. XCTest's host never takes it, so a person's copy never defers to a test host. A first draft deferred to any running process with the app's bundle identifier and activated it. With that design two copies launched together could both quit, a person's copy launched during a test run deferred to the test host, and the activation showed nothing for a menu bar app with no window open. The lock does not cover a copy launched while the old one is still exiting. Replacing an older running build stays an install or swap step's job: quit it, wait for the exit, then open the new build by path. Conflab's CLI will also read the lock, to tell whether the app runs, so Conflab documents the file, the lock and the bytes its holder writes as a contract (its ST0125 design, decision 7), under which a reader probes with a shared lock and never creates the file. A guard that arca_swift carries keeps that contract, or says where it differs.

**Who it hits:** every estate menubar app: Gtools.app, menuz, Intent.app and Conflab.app.

**The ask:** arca_swift carries each of them, so that adopters stop copying them: the two masthead fixes inside `MastheadRow` or the call that makes it, and the test-host check and the guard as one launch-time call that an adopter's `applicationDidFinishLaunching` makes first. Each adopter's copy carries a pointer to this issue and goes once arca_swift ships its replacement.

**Size:** S.

Resolution: Fixed in 0.3.0 (tag d6b053ec on 940f91b5), STc203646d7444f4f1; CI run 45765409791 green
